Frequentist Variance of a Fit

Source: R/inference_objects.R
frequentist_vcov.Rd

Selects the sandwich variance \(V_f = (H+S)^{-1} H (H+S)^{-1}\), with \(H\) the information of the log-likelihood and \(S\) the second derivative of the penalty. It is the sampling variance of the penalized estimator at a fixed penalty, conditional on the hyperparameters.

Usage

frequentist_vcov(information = NULL, sandwich = NULL)

Arguments

information

NULL (the default) or the matrix \(H\), an object that inherits from distributions7::Information:

  • NULL: the matrix is chosen for each fit by the family of the fit, as distributions7::observed_info() where the log-likelihood is twice differentiable in every parameter of the family (every distributions7::params_order() is at least 2), and as distributions7::expected_info() with method = NULL, for the whole matrix, otherwise. The families with a kink in a parameter, such as the Laplace, have a singular observed information in that parameter and take the expected one;

  • distributions7::observed_info(): the negative Hessian of the log-likelihood at the data;

  • distributions7::expected_info(): the Fisher information, whose method is NULL (the closed form of the family where it has one, distributions7::expect_opg() otherwise) or one of distributions7::expect_opg(), distributions7::expect_integrate() and distributions7::expect_mc() (see distributions7::expected_derivative_methods).

auto_info() is not accepted. For a model with a structural term, see vcov_method. The choice does not depend on how the fit was computed (inner_information of statmod()). summary.StatmodFit() states the matrix when it is not the observed one, and a printed variance object states the information that it names. information_objects compares the objects.

sandwich

NULL (the default) or an object from hc0_sandwich(), hc1_sandwich() or hac_sandwich(). NULL keeps \(H\) as the meat, the matrix above. Otherwise the meat is built from the scores of the observations and the matrix is the robust sandwich variance described at hc0_sandwich(), or the HAC variance for dependent observations described at hac_sandwich().

Value

A FrequentistVcov object, inheriting from vcov_method, with the property name equal to "frequentist" and the properties information and sandwich.

Details

The matrix is smaller than the Bayesian one wherever there is a penalty, because it omits the smoothing bias, and an interval built from it covers less. With no penalty it equals \(H^{-1}\). See vcov_method for the three conventions side by side and vcov.StatmodFit() for the matrices in full.

See also

bayesian_vcov() and unconditional_vcov() for the siblings, vcov_method for the comparison, and vcov.StatmodFit(), confint.StatmodFit(), summary.StatmodFit() and statmod_test() for the functions that take it.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(80))
dd$y <- 1 + 2 * dd$x + rnorm(80, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
frequentist_vcov()
#> <vcov> frequentist
vcov(fit, vcov_type = frequentist_vcov())
#>                   mu:(Intercept)          mu:x sigma:(Intercept)
#> mu:(Intercept)      7.691473e-03 -1.161719e-02      8.809850e-19
#> mu:x               -1.161719e-02  2.209835e-02      3.360036e-18
#> sigma:(Intercept)   8.809850e-19  3.360036e-18      6.410256e-03
summary(fit, vcov_type = frequentist_vcov())
#> A statmod fit
#> 
#> Call:  statmod(formula = y ~ x, distrib = distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), 
#>             data = dd)
#> 
#> Distribution: gaussian1     Observations: 80
#> 
#> === mu   [identity link]
#> 
#> Parametric terms
#>                estimate     se     z       p  lower upper
#>   (Intercept)     1.043 0.0877  11.9 < 1e-16 0.8714 1.215
#>   x               2.008 0.1487 13.51 < 1e-16  1.716 2.299
#> 
#> === sigma   [log link]
#> 
#> Parametric terms
#>                estimate      se     z       p lower   upper
#>   (Intercept)    -1.033 0.08006 -12.9 < 1e-16 -1.19 -0.8759
#> 
#> 95% intervals, frequentist variance
#> conditional log-likelihood -29.891019    effective df 3.00
#> cAIC 65.782    cBIC 72.928
#> fitted in 89 ms
#> inner   max |grad|/se 5.3e-15   min eigen 0.11
#> outer   max |grad|/se 9.4e-15   min eigen 1
frequentist_vcov(information = distributions7::expected_info())
#> <vcov> frequentist (expected information)
frequentist_vcov(sandwich = hc1_sandwich())
#> <vcov> frequentist with HC1 sandwich
